questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Triple Integrals by Changing the Projection Type
questions.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{xy}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$*
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le xy}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{xy}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/6b3720af66e81aef6792d4b2a34b2bdf2b93bd59ed6e28e4b38a1e06964bb2cc.png)

The region $D$ is type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,x\le y\le 1}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
x=0
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
y=x\,⟹\,x=y.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le y},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/9dc99cc0df9f089b9f62402c3c5ea9c4408be077debbf6dfadeb884ee4d8b2d0.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{xy}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{xy}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}[{\int }_{0}^{xy}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})[z]_{0}^{xy}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})[{\int }_{0}^{y}2x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})[{x}^{2}]_{0}^{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{4})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{4})]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-1) \\  & =\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Triple Integrals by Changing the Projection Type
questions.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$*
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\,0\le z\le {e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/38eb7316b1ee5c947eee37a9cc10530ff08f793b7564cf0d88c6ce24e1239f9d.png)

The region $D$ is type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
y=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \operatorname{sin}⁡x},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/241abff7fae5d6ba3301d605ff4c4e62ff61e423515c7bc3a54b17b9aec525aa.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}[{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\text{d}z]\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}[z]_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}[y]_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =[-{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}]_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-({e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi /2}-{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡0}) \\  & =-(1-e) \\  & =e-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned
questions.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{z}}^{{e}^{z}}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{p}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{q}{\int }_{r}^{1}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(x)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,z)}^{{u}_{4}(x,z)}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{z}\le x\le {e}^{z},\,\,{z}^{2}-1\le y\le x+z}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{z}}^{{e}^{z}}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(x)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/41b06d98498273a03b9df8eeaa60f4e74cb00168e8dd0b3b395c5b0a23518e57.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\sqrt{z}\le x\le {e}^{z}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/07a37b90df8b37d07c40af03ecba8e665797cfff368758db7ae17e45f11683cf.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ are

$\,$ $z=0\,$ and $\,z={x}^{2}.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ are

$\,$ $z=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,$ and $\,z=1.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le {x}^{2}}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,z)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡x\le z\le 1}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}^{1}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{(x+1)^{3}}^{2-{x}^{2}}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{p}{\int }_{q}^{\sqrt[3]{z}-1}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{r}^{0}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,z)}^{{u}_{4}(x,z)}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,\,(x+1)^{3}\le z\le 2-{x}^{2},\,\,x+z\le y\le z+2}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{(x+1)^{3}}^{2-{x}^{2}}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(z)}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/5f586edef4202e3f3de09fe947c955de62efa35e421e85b3e5034efd375790a7.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,(x+1)^{3}\le z\le 2-{x}^{2}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/ec9845e347959ff1ac43a12d03261b1eb31172f14b56269d7bbfcb86a2a23e48.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(z),$ are

$\,$ $x=-1\,$ and $\,x=\sqrt[3]{z}-1.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(z),$ are

$\,$ $x=-\sqrt{2-z}\,$ and $\,x=0.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,-1\le x\le \sqrt[3]{z}-1}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 2,\,-\sqrt{2-z}\le x\le 0}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{\sqrt[3]{z}-1}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-\sqrt{2-z}}^{0}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Triple Integrals by Changing the Projection Type
questions.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{z}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}z{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.$*
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}z{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,z\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{3}}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}z{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/54d8420870ea92e42811a13ed2c4563c5c9ccb674ee8c3b6a277186c0fba21da.png)

The region $D$ is type II region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,z\le x\le 1}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $z=z(x),$ is

$$
x=z\,⟹\,z=x
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
z=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le x},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/7f19b63139a3d38c321e9938c1e8fbbf84e924df51d9b9b057d0151fc269550d.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{z}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}z{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}z{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}[z{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}z[{e}^{y}]_{0}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}z({e}^{{x}^{3}}-1)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[({e}^{{x}^{3}}-1){\int }_{0}^{x}z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{{x}^{3}}-1){[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{0}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}({e}^{{x}^{3}}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{3}}-{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{1}{3}{e}^{{x}^{3}}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[e-1-1+0] \\  & =\frac{e-2}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
